name: TowerPro MG996R
description: Standard-size metal-gear PWM hobby servo, an upgraded MG995 commonly used for robot-arm and hexapod joints.

specs.label: Current
specs.value: 10 mA idle, 170 mA no-load, 1400 mA stall

specs.label: Interface
specs.value: PWM, JR plug (fits JR and Futaba), 1 µs dead band, 32 cm lead

specs.label: Gears
specs.value: Metal (TowerPro says gear set and shaft upgraded to 6061-T6 aluminium)

envelope.axes: x = case length (B), y = width (D), z = case height excl. output spline (C), from TowerPro's 'Product configure table'

notes: TowerPro publishes no CAD, no mechanical drawing and no datasheet PDF. Its /download/ page is empty, and the product page gives only a spec list plus a lettered 'configure table' (A–F) keyed to a generic image (saved as docs/dim_key.jpg). Mapping the letters to features is my reading of that key image: A = overall height incl. spline, B = case length, C = height excl. spline, D = width, E = tab-to-tab length, F = bottom to tab. Mount-critical values (tab hole pitch and diameter, shaft offset, spline teeth, screw sizes) are not published by TowerPro, so they are null; measure a genuine unit or use a community model. The widely shared 'MG996R Tower-Pro' PDF (e.g. people.ece.cornell.edu/.../MG996RTowerPro.pdf) was printed by a reseller with Bullzip in 2014. It is not a TowerPro file and gives different values (0.17/0.14 s, 4.8–7.2 V, 2.5 A stall), so it was not used. TowerPro warns that many MG996Rs sold on Amazon/eBay/Alibaba are counterfeits. The Amazon pick is sold by American Robotic Supply, which describes itself as a Tower Pro dealer; its title verified, but the page showed no buy box, so it may be unavailable. A 360° continuous version from the same seller: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B081XC2BM4 ('Tower Pro MG996R 360° Rotation Robotic Servo', verified).
